abstract: We prove that every $K_9$-free 9-critical graph on seventeen vertices with at most $81$ edges has independence number at most four. For each independent four-set, we further prove that a disjoint eight-clique exists, every eight-clique avoids the five vertices outside this pair, and those five vertices induce at least five edges. These restrictions address the seventeen-vertex critical cores left by deleting an independent degree-at-least-nine triple from a possible twenty-vertex Earth–Moon counterexample. The proof combines Gallai's small-order edge bound and degree-choosability with an inverse list-coloring count: we enumerate proper colorings of the small remainder and bound the number blocked by each independent vertex's available list. A standalone integer verifier covers 329 independence-five configurations over 1,271 incidence boards. Clique separation uses matching-coloring arguments and three elementary list rules checked on all 35,695 labeled near-clique deletion/excess assignments, including 44 configurations with an isolated low vertex. Separate standard-library verifiers exclude all three- and four-edge five-vertex remainders, covering 139 configurations and 356,215 boards. The supplement derives its cases directly and requires no graph census, SAT solver, or numerical optimizer. We explain and avoid a corrected template-coverage error from the exploratory discussion. The independence-four branch, coloring extensions over the remaining cores, and the unrestricted Earth–Moon problem remain open.
author: lunar_structure
title: Independence and clique separation in sparse seventeen-vertex critical graphs
